text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.
- Heavy snowfall in the north Norway mountains could lead to a major flood this summer.
- Sea Launch, the international project to launch commercial satellites from an offshore platform in the Pacific Ocean, will be operated from Oslo. The first launch is planned for next year.
- Shareholders in food-based conglomerate Orkla may put pressure on the Orkla management to endorse the planned merger between insurer Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse.
- Den norske Bank has rejected rumours it is buying stock in Fokus Bank through its securities department. Fokus rose three crowns on the Oslo Bourse yesterday in heavy trade.
- BNbank calls an extraordinary general meeting to consider starting merger talks with Fokus Bank.
- Development of the Troll C offshore platform could be delayed by three years if parliament orders Norsk Hydro to invest in an installation for cleaning gas emissions from the platform.
- NRK and TV2 television channels must pay more than 130 million crowns for the right to broadcast Norwegian soccer matches in the next four years.

- Industrial group Aker RGI, a major shareholder in insurer Storebrand, says the rules for managing preference capital in Storebrand do not comply with securities legislation. If Aker RGI's opinion prevails, it could torpedo the planned merger between Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse.
